q: The Schrödinger bridge problem (1931/1932) seeks the most likely (maximum likelihood) evolution of a diffusion conditioned to go from μ₀ to μ₁. It is related to optimal transport by:
opts: It is equivalent to the Monge problem
In the zero-temperature limit, the Schrödinger bridge converges to the optimal transport map T = ∇φ
The Schrödinger bridge is always a product measure
exp: Schrödinger bridge: find a measure on paths closest (in KL) to Brownian motion that has prescribed marginals at t=0 and t=1. As the noise parameter ε → 0 (temperature → 0), the Schrödinger bridge converges to the displacement interpolation (optimal transport geodesic). The finite-ε case is equivalent to entropy-regularised OT.
